verdict: Caution — lend only to BESS/EPC and O&M contractors with proven execution and escrowed receivables; avoid pure merchant solar/wind SPVs in Jaisalmer until PPA tenure and DSCR data are on file.
title: Jaisalmer Renewables (solar/wind): a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Jaisalmer renewable borrower is either a generation SPV (panels or turbines on desert land, selling units under a PPA) or a contractor servicing that build-out. **Generation is capital-heavy with near-flat opex, so cash comes from units sold, not from the asset** [9]. Revenue is single-part tariff and moves with wind speed and weather, so a weak-monsoon or low-wind quarter hits cash directly [9][10]. **Contractors earn on execution milestones, so their cash sits in receivables and retention, not in plant.**

## What has changed now
Local news is thin and mostly one project: GEON commissioned a 10 MW / 20 MWh battery system in Jaisalmer to support renewable integration and grid stability [1][2]. That tells us storage is arriving here, but it is a single commissioning, not a market. **Peer results are mixed: Suzlon revenue grew 26% to Rs 4,869 crore in Q2 FY27 while EBITDA margin narrowed to 14.8% from 18.6%** [4][5]; GK Energy's H1 FY27 revenue grew 38.9% to Rs 907.8 crore with a 150 MW/300 MWh BESS order [6]; Waaree faced lower module utilisation and softer module prices [7]. **Read this as volume growth with margin squeeze — good for contractors, tight for manufacturers.** Rating reports (undated) flag floating-rate term loans and PPA lock-in shorter than debt tenure [8][11].

## Where to grow
Pursue BESS EPC and O&M contractors riding the storage build [1][2][6], and rooftop/C&I solar installers with a 1 lakh-unit order book type of visibility [6]. **Avoid merchant solar/wind SPVs with no PPA tenure on file and single-asset borrowers whose entire cash flow is one tariff stream** [9][10]. When a proposal lands, check PPA lock-in against loan tenure; if lock-in is shorter, ask for the sponsor's re-contracting track record [8][11].

## How to grow safely
Structure against DSCR, not asset value: **take a cash trap at DSCR below 1.10x, as the ReNew covenant does** [10]. Require P-90 PLF evidence post-commissioning, since sustained design PLF is the key monitorable [11]. Collect from customer: PPA tariff, PPA tenure, DSCR, PLF history, receivables ageing. **Every month take: generation/PLF report, receivable ageing, DSCR certificate, and confirmation of floating-rate reset** [8][9].

## Early warning
- PLF below design P-90 for two quarters (monthly) -> freeze further drawdown, re-run DSCR [11].
- Receivables past 90 days from a single discom (monthly) -> shift to escrow, cut limit [10].
- PPA lock-in expiring within loan tenor (quarterly) -> demand re-contracting evidence [8].
- Interest reset raising instalment (quarterly) -> re-test DSCR headroom [8].
- Margin compression at the contractor's client (quarterly) -> tighten retention release [4][7].
